London, 2<sup>nd</sup> April 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**Ford and GM** posted the sharpest declines among the major automakers as U.S. sales fell 36.8% in March.  Ford’s sales dropped 42.1% and GM’s 44.7%- GM’s fifth slide of more than 40% in the past six months. Chrysler sales tumbled 39.3%, its smallest percentage slide since October. The biggest Japanese automakers all fell between 36 and 39%.  The results exceeded analysts’ projections and were aided by record-high incentive spending. The seasonally adjusted annual rate of 9.3 million bested February’s 27year low of 9.1 million.  Some analysts and company officials said they saw signals that the worst of the industry’s 17-month streak of declines may have passed.   Ford said it built 349,000 vehicles in the first quarter, 26,000 fewer than estimated in its latest forecast. Honda’s March decline was 36.3%; Nissan North America’s, 37.7%; and Toyota Motor Sales U.S.A.’s, 39%. BMW of North America’s 22.9% decline was better than President Jim O’Donnell expected. Last year, 13.2 million light vehicles were sold in the United States. Through 2008, the average this decade was 16.4 million annually. _Source:  Automotive News_ 

**In a report** sent to the U.S. Treasury Department, **GM** adjusted its planned losses before interest and taxes to deteriorate by an additional $1.1 billion this year compared with a forecast released Feb. 17. But GM forecasts that cash burn will improve by $700 million this year.  GM said 2009 adjusted earnings before interest and taxes, or EBIT, would show a loss of $6.3 billion, compared with its Feb. 17 forecast loss of $5.2 billion. GM’s 2008 EBIT was a loss of $8.1 billion.  GM reported it that burned through $12 billion in 2008. In its Feb. 17 viability plan to Treasury, GM estimated the cash burn at $8.2 billion for this year. It is now lowering that forecast to $7.5 billion. _Source:  Automotive News_ 

**France’s** three domestic car brands increased new-car sales in their home market by 14.6% in March, according to the French car manufacturers association, CCFA. Government-funded scrapping incentives and rebates for low-CO2 cars boosted demand for the small, fuel-efficient models produced by Renault, Peugeot and Citroen.  PSA/Peugeot-Citroen two brands increased car sales by 15.9 % in March to 66,204. Citroen showed the strongest performance, with its March sales up 28.6 % to 32,772 units.  Peugeot’s car sales grew by 5.7 % to 33,432 units, but the brand’s market share fell to 16.4 % from 16.7 %.  Renault’s new-car registrations in March were up 12.9 % to 54,256.  CCFA President Xavier Fels said 30% to 40 % of all new-car sales in France were linked to a government-funded 1,000 euro incentive for buyers who scrap 10-year-old cars.  Foreign brands also improved; Fiat increased sales by 20.5 % to 7,876 units. Volkswagen group registered a 15.3 % increase in sales to 22,380 units, largely attributed to the VW brand.  Ford of Europe’s French sales

up 3.6 % to 11,476 units.   Opel saw sales drop by 22.7 % to 6,970 units.  Toyota’s French sales were down 4.9 % in to 8,472 units.  BMW, Mercedes-Benz, and Nissan each recorded double-digit declines during March. _Source:  Automotive News Europe_ 

**Eastplats** recorded a net loss of $5,742,000 ($0.01 loss/share) compared to a net loss of $10,814,000 ($0.02 loss/ share) in Q4 07.  Production at the Crocodile River Mine increased by 9% to 29,015 PGM ounces, from 26,632 PGM ounces in Q4 07.  The company acquired an additional direct and indirect 2.47% interest in Barplats Investments Limited, the subsidiary that holds CRM and Kennedy’s Vale. _Source:  Eastplats_ 

**North American Palladium** (NAP) has agreed to buy gold exploration firm Cadiscor Resources in an all-share transaction.  The company said last month it wants to buy gold mines.  Cadiscor is exploring for gold on several properties in Quebec, and last year acquired Sleeping Giant from Iamgold.  Cadiscor said in February that it planned to start production at Sleeping Giant in Q3 09, at a rate of 50koz/y. _Source:  Mining Weekly_
